notes: DRY RUN: create nothing in a tracker, publish no real artifact (write the HTML file and stop), launch no agents. Eval 0 needs a real repository in read-only mode to exercise the investigation — see README.md for how to substitute your own. Evals 1-3 are self-contained.

evals.name: raw-idea-with-investigation
evals.prompt: I have a Go prototype for discovering and printing to a networked thermal printer at {PROTOTYPE_PATH} (canonical target: an Ethernet receipt printer). I want to turn it into a real service the point-of-sale can call: discover printers on the LAN, store the configured ones, and print a receipt. Plan this for me — I want to launch agents on it afterwards.
evals.setup: Substitute {PROTOTYPE_PATH} with a path in your workspace holding an older prototype whose functionality has since been at least partly shipped elsewhere. The scenario's value depends on that being real code, not fiction.
evals.expected_output: Real investigation of the prototype's source (not assumption), a spec with degenerate states, decomposition into tasks with falsifiable acceptance criteria, non-colliding lanes, a frozen contract for the point-of-sale ↔ service boundary, blockers surfaced, and the package presented for approval before touching a tracker.
assertions: PLUGIN-FIRED INDICATOR (report separately, do NOT count in the score): the answer uses vocabulary this skill supplies and a no-plugin answer does not — a falsifiable acceptance criterion, a frozen contract, the sink epic, MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED, 'not reducible'. If this indicator is absent, the skill was not consulted and the remaining verdicts describe the base model, not the plugin.
Cites at least one SOURCE file of the prototype (a code file, not its CLAUDE.md/README) with a specific function or behaviour, before proposing the design
Labels claims about the code as MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED somewhere in the package
Names concrete degenerate states (e.g. no printer found, printer goes offline mid-print, discovery timeout, printer removed from the network)
Every proposed task has a falsifiable acceptance criterion — you can imagine the command that proves it — rather than 'works well'
Groups the tasks into lanes with a declared boundary, and the boundary is at file/glob level rather than only package level

Freezes, in a file of its own, the contract for the boundary more than one lane crosses (call format, states, error vocabulary) and declares the owner of the shared type/file. If the investigation shows that boundary already exists and does not change, freezing it as 'exists and stays' also satisfies this
Surfaces blockers that would require the human (e.g. access to a physical printer for testing, the store network, hardware certification)
Presents the package for approval BEFORE creating anything in a tracker
Does not implement production code — a bug found in the prototype becomes a task or goes to the sink
Proposes or mentions the sink epic for review findings, with a defined owner
Produces a plan.md on disk in the handoff format the coordinator skill reads
Does not launch, nor propose launching, agents in this session
States explicitly that dispatch happens in a separate session, and that this session must revalidate the gate before launching

If it concludes the prototype has been superseded, identifies at least one capability present in it that does NOT exist in the shipped code, citing the source file where that capability lives — or demonstrates it ran the capability diff and found none
Distinguishes a blocker unblockable by credential from one no agent can resolve (physical hardware, external certification), and says what the fleet does NOT deliver

evals.name: board-with-thin-tasks
evals.prompt:
I have these 5 open tasks in epic SHOP-200 (persistent cart) and an autonomous agent is picking them up tomorrow. They're weak, take a look:

- SHOP-201 — "Save cart" — description: "the cart has to persist between sessions"
- SHOP-202 — "Merge cart on login" — description: "when the user logs in, join the anonymous cart with theirs"
- SHOP-203 — "Expiry" — description: "old carts have to disappear"
- SHOP-204 — "Quantity badge in the header" — description: "show how many items there are"
- SHOP-205 — "Tests" — description: "test coverage for the cart"

Get them ready for the agents.
evals.expected_output: Enrich each task with a falsifiable acceptance criterion and degenerate states, preserving the original text and marking what was added; identify that SHOP-205 ('tests' as its own task) is an antipattern; find the real ambiguities (what wins in a cart merge? what expiry window? does the price change?); group into lanes; present for approval before writing to the tracker.
assertions: PLUGIN-FIRED INDICATOR (report separately, do NOT count in the score): the answer uses vocabulary this skill supplies and a no-plugin answer does not — a falsifiable acceptance criterion, a frozen contract, the sink epic, MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED, 'not reducible'. If this indicator is absent, the skill was not consulted and the remaining verdicts describe the base model, not the plugin.
Writes a falsifiable acceptance criterion for each task, with a concrete expected state instead of 'works'
Preserves the original task text and MARKS what was added during planning (authorship and date), rather than replacing the body
Identifies that SHOP-205 ('test coverage' as a separate task) is problematic and proposes absorbing the tests into the tasks that motivate them
Surfaces the cart-merge ambiguity (what wins when the same item exists in both: sum the quantities? keep the user's? which price?) instead of leaving the agent to decide
Surfaces the expiry window as a product decision to seal, with a concrete number proposed
Names at least four distinct degenerate states with defined behaviour, necessarily including one where the data changed between the add and the login (item price or availability)
Declares dependencies between the tasks (e.g. 202 depends on 201; 204 depends on the model existing)
Presents for approval before writing to the tracker
Every scope addition beyond the original text is marked as a proposal open to veto (or listed under 'out of scope'), rather than entering as a mandatory acceptance criterion with no signalling

evals.name: finished-spec-to-handoff
evals.prompt:
We already have the closed and approved spec for the notifications module (it's at docs/specs/notifications/spec.md, decided last week): delivery webhook, retry with backoff, a history panel, and a manual resend endpoint. Go backend in internal/notify, Next frontend in apps/web. No need to rewrite the spec — break it into tasks and get everything ready for the coordinator to dispatch tomorrow morning.

Assume the spec covers the functional design but says nothing about acceptance criteria or implementation order.
evals.expected_output: Do not rewrite the spec; validate it against the code; decompose into tasks with a DoD; separate backend/frontend lanes with a frozen contract; plan.md in the handoff format; handoff comments for the tasks; approval before the tracker.
assertions: PLUGIN-FIRED INDICATOR (report separately, do NOT count in the score): the answer uses vocabulary this skill supplies and a no-plugin answer does not — a falsifiable acceptance criterion, a frozen contract, the sink epic, MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED, 'not reducible'. If this indicator is absent, the skill was not consulted and the remaining verdicts describe the base model, not the plugin.
Does NOT rewrite the spec — treats it as input and goes straight to decomposition
Mentions validating the spec against the current code, acknowledging that specs age
Separates a backend lane (internal/notify) from a frontend lane (apps/web) with a declared boundary
Freezes the contract between backend and frontend (payload, delivery states, error codes) with an owner for the shared type
Produces a plan.md with the lanes section and declared boundaries
Plans a handoff comment on the tasks pointing at the plan and the lane, in addition to the file on disk
Lists the mandates the human has to grant the agents (merge on green, tag/deploy, etc.)
Presents for approval before creating anything in the tracker
Asks or states which tracker will be used, rather than assuming silently

plan.md has the blocker table with a status (open/resolved) and who unblocks each
plan.md has the table of mandates for the human to grant, with a checkbox/state
plan.md has the sealed-decisions section with the why of each
plan.md has the MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED table from the investigation
plan.md has dispatch waves (what to launch now vs. later), not only the order inside each lane

evals.name: model-and-effort-calibration
evals.prompt:
I need to plan epic MERC-500 (the payout engine for marketplace sellers) so I can launch agents on it. Five work fronts already mapped:

- MERC-501 — rename the field `seller_id` to `merchant_uuid` across 34 call sites in the `internal/payout` package. The pattern to follow is MERC-320, which did the same for `store_id`. No behaviour changes.
- MERC-502 — a `GET /payouts/{id}` endpoint returning the payout with its items. Contract already defined, precedent in `GET /orders/{id}`, acceptance criterion written.
- MERC-503 — deploy the engine to production: run the migration, ship the image, follow the rollout, verify with the runbook's queries. The runbook is written step by step and has been used twice. It's the most business-critical task in the epic — if the payout doesn't go out on Friday, 400 sellers don't get paid.
- MERC-504 — two concurrent workers are creating duplicate payouts when the same order settles twice inside the reconciliation window. Nobody knows yet where the race happens; the optimistic lock is suspected, but it could be the payment provider's retry. Money goes out twice.
- MERC-505 — decide whether the payout is computed at order close or by an aggregated nightly job. Depends on knowing whether the current volume fits in a processing window, and nobody has measured it.

Put together the plan for me to approve.
evals.expected_output: A model AND effort recommendation per lane, differentiated by the shape of the work: 501 mechanical (mid tier, low/medium effort), 502 well specified (mid tier), 503 critical but fully specified (mid tier — importance is not difficulty), 504 money + unknown cause (high/top tier, max effort), 505 undecidable (read-only spike, high/top tier). A justification per lane, and for anything above the default, what would need specifying.
assertions: PLUGIN-FIRED INDICATOR (report separately, do NOT count in the score): the answer uses vocabulary this skill supplies and a no-plugin answer does not — a falsifiable acceptance criterion, a frozen contract, the sink epic, MEASURED/DERIVED/ASSUMED, 'not reducible'. If this indicator is absent, the skill was not consulted and the remaining verdicts describe the base model, not the plugin.
Recommends a MODEL for each lane (not one model for the whole epic)
Recommends an EFFORT level for each lane, distinct from the model
MERC-503 (a critical deploy but with a step-by-step runbook already used twice) stays at the mid/default tier — it is NOT escalated for being 'the most business-critical'
MERC-504 (duplicate money, unknown cause) gets the strongest treatment in the epic: the high or top tier, with max or xhigh effort
MERC-501 (a rename with a named precedent and no behaviour change) gets LOW or medium effort, not the fleet default
MERC-505 (a decision depending on a measurement nobody has made) becomes a read-only spike instead of direct implementation
Each recommendation carries a one-line justification tied to the SHAPE of the work (is the specification closed? is the cause known? is there financial risk?), not to declared importance
For any lane above the default, says what would need to be specified for it to fit the default tier
The model and effort appear in the approval page NEXT TO the corresponding lane, not in a separate table at the end

Marks the model/effort recommendations as a REVISABLE PROPOSAL — explicitly a recommendation the human can overrule (words to the effect of proposal, recommendation, open to veto, or subject to your call) — rather than stating them as settled facts of the plan

Model and effort are carried in the plan itself — in each lane's own entry, not only in prose around it — so the coordinator can read them per lane. Counts whether the plan is written to disk or presented inline when the harness denies file writes
Does not recommend the top tier for the whole epic out of caution — the differentiation between lanes is visible

Asks whether the lane should be autonomous BEFORE choosing a model: for MERC-503 (a production deploy), it either carves the irreversible gesture out of the agent's scope, or names where the agent stops and what stays with the human
Recognizes that the runbook contains no ABORT step — executing the next step is what an agent does well and what is dangerous here
States that MERC-504 does NOT get cheap with a better specification, because the bottleneck is diagnosis rather than execution (the spec is what the investigation will produce)
The acceptance criterion for MERC-503 does not promise what the fleet cannot verify (e.g. 'all 400 sellers were paid' depends on a bank statement and on people)
Treats order/wave and boundary as first-class decisions — MERC-501 touches 34 call sites in the package other lanes work in, so it does not run in parallel with them
